# Business Events

## When to Use This Skill

Use this skill when the user wants to:
- Define event-driven APIs using Kafka/message brokers
- Create business event services that publish events
- View or describe existing business event services
- Set up publish/subscribe message channels

## Commands

### View Business Events

```sql
-- List all business event service documents
list business event services;

-- Filter by module
list business event services in MyModule;

-- List all business event client documents (future)
list business event clients;

-- List individual messages across all services
list business events;

-- Filter messages by module
list business events in MyModule;

-- Full MDL description (round-trippable for a PUBLISHED service)
describe business event service Module.ServiceName;
```

`list business event services` has a **Kind** column: `published` (a definition of its
own) or `consumed` (no definition, the producer's AsyncAPI contract cached instead). A
consumed service shows 0 messages because its messages live in the contract, not in a
definition — the kind is what makes that legible. `list business events` lists both
roles' events with the **Channel** the broker derives the topic from.

### Author a Consumed Service

A **consumed** service stores the producing app's AsyncAPI contract instead of a
definition of its own, and binds events from it:

```sql
mdl 1;
create or modify business event service Module.OrdersEventClient
(
  ContractFile: 'contracts/OrdersEventService.yaml'   -- or Contract: $$<yaml>$$
)
{
  consume OrderPlaceEvent (Entity: Module.CBE_OrderPlaceEvent, Microflow: Module.HandleBE_OrderPlaceEvent);
};
```

- Exactly one of `Contract:` / `ContractFile:`, and neither may be mixed with
  `ServiceName`, `EventNamePrefix` or `message` — those are the published shape.
- `ContractFile` is read when the script runs and stored **verbatim**, so nothing later
  depends on the file. `describe` prints the `Contract:` form, which re-executes anywhere.
- It is `consume`, not `subscribe`: `message X (…) subscribe` already means "this app
  consumes X of its *own* definition". The stored `Operation` is `"subscribe"` either
  way; only the keyword differs.
- The consumed entity (`CBE_…`, extending `BusinessEvents.ConsumedBusinessEvent`) and the
  handler microflow are ordinary MDL, declared before the service.
- A service whose contract contains `$$` cannot be described inline — `$$…$$` has no
  escape — so `describe` falls back to comments and tells you to use `ContractFile`.

A published-shaped statement over a stored contract is still refused rather than allowed
to destroy it (ako/mxcli#2381).

### Two Apps: Export the Contract, Then Consume It

The producing app mints the channel id and it reaches the consumer **inside the exported
contract** — not by both apps spelling the same string. `export contract` writes the
document Studio Pro's *Export AsyncAPI Document* button produces:

```bash
mxcli export contract CdcPublish.OrdersEventService -p appA.mpr -o contract.yaml
```

Then name that file in app B's script (`ContractFile: 'contract.yaml'`). Both apps then
show the same Channel in `list business events`, which is what the broker derives the
topic from.

Only business event services export so far. A published OData or REST service's contract
is served by the running app, so exporting one means fetching rather than rendering it.

Payload types: only `Long` is measured against a Studio Pro export, so the renderer
refuses the others rather than guess (#2384 §9.1) — export from Studio Pro and use
`ContractFile:` for a service that uses them.

### Create a Business Event Service

```sql
mdl 1;
create business event service Module.CustomerEventsApi
(
  ServiceName: 'CustomerEventsApi',
  EventNamePrefix: 'com.example'
)
{
  message CustomerChangedEvent (CustomerId: long) {
    publish (Entity: Module.PBE_CustomerChangedEvent);
  };
  message AddressChangedEvent (AddressId: long) {
    publish (Entity: Module.PBE_AddressChangedEvent);
  };
};
```

### Create or Modify (Idempotent Update — Preferred)

Preserves the existing UUID so other documents that reference this service remain valid.
`OR REPLACE` is accepted as a synonym. Each message keeps its stored channel — the
channel name is what the broker derives the Kafka topic from
(`businessevents.<channel id>.<space>`) — matched by message name, so a re-run of an
unchanged script reports `Unchanged`; only a new message gets a new (random) channel
name. Renaming a message is a new channel.

There is no MDL property to state a channel name, and that is correct: the producing app
mints the id, and it reaches a consumer **inside the exported AsyncAPI contract**, not by
both apps spelling the same string. Read it with `list business events` (Channel column)
or `show contract channels from Module.Service`, which works on a publisher as well as a
consumer.

```sql
mdl 1;
create or modify business event service Module.CustomerEventsApi
(
  ServiceName: 'CustomerEventsApi',
  EventNamePrefix: ''
)
{
  message CustomerChangedEvent (CustomerId: long) {
    publish (Entity: Module.PBE_CustomerChangedEvent);
  };
};
```

### Drop a Business Event Service

```sql
mdl 1;
drop business event service Module.CustomerEventsApi;
```

## Message Definition Syntax

A message's operations are its children, each with its properties in `( )`:

```
message <MessageName> (<AttrName>: <type>, ...) {
  publish (Entity: <Module.PBE_Entity>);
  subscribe (Entity: <Module.CBE_Entity>, Microflow: <Module.Handler>);
};
```

Give a message the operations it has: `publish` only, `subscribe` only, or both, for
a message the app publishes and consumes itself (an in-app bus, a request/reply loop).

Declare a message **once**. The same name declared twice (once per operation) stores
two messages of one name, which `mx check` accepts and the deployment rejects ("An item
with the same key has already been added"); `check` refuses it.

The keyword clauses `message X (…) publish entity M.E microflow M.H;` and
`consume X entity M.E microflow M.H;` are the old spelling (MDL-DEPR075, MDL-DEPR076):
they still run, warn, and `mxcli fmt --upgrade` rewrites them.

### Supported Attribute Types
- `string`, `string(n)`, `string(unlimited)` - Text. The length must match the
  linked entity attribute's; a bare `string` stores no length, which the build
  reads as 200
- `integer` - 32-bit integer
- `long` - 64-bit integer
- `decimal` - Precise decimal number
- `boolean` - True/false
- `datetime` - Date and time

## Service Properties

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `ServiceName` | The service name used in the event broker |
| `EventNamePrefix` | Prefix added to event names (can be empty) |
| `folder` | Optional folder path for the service document |

## Operations

| Operation | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `publish` | This service publishes the event (other apps subscribe) |
| `subscribe` | This service subscribes to the event (other apps publish) |
| both | One message the app publishes and consumes: a `publish` and a `subscribe` child |

## Publishing Events from Microflows

There is no dedicated microflow activity for publishing business events. Instead, Mendix
provides Java actions in the `BusinessEvents` marketplace module. Use `call java action`
to publish an event from a microflow:

```sql
-- Create an event entity instance and publish it
create microflow Module.ACT_PublishCustomerChanged
  folder 'ACT'
begin
  $event = create Module.PBE_CustomerChangedEvent (CustomerId = $CustomerId);
  commit $event;
  call java action BusinessEvents.PublishBusinessEvent_V2(
    Subject = 'Customer {1} changed' with ({1} = $CustomerId),
    BusinessEvent = $event
  );
end;
```

`PublishBusinessEvent_V2` takes two parameters: `Subject`, a **text template**
(`StringTemplate(Text)`), and `BusinessEvent`, the event object. `Subject` is
written like a log message — a string, or `'… {1} …' with ({1} = …)`; each
argument must be a String, Integer, Decimal, Boolean or DateTime value (wrap an
enumeration in `getCaption(…)`). `describe java action` shows the parameters of
any action before you call it.

### Available Java Actions (from BusinessEvents module)

| Java Action | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `BusinessEvents.PublishBusinessEvent_V2` | Publish an event (recommended) |
| `BusinessEvents.PublishBusinessEvent` | Publish an event (legacy) |
| `BusinessEvents.ConsumeBusinessEvent` | Consume/acknowledge an event |
| `BusinessEvents.PublishEvents` | Publish multiple events |
| `BusinessEvents.StartupBusinessEvents` | Initialize the event broker connection |
| `BusinessEvents.ShutdownBusinessEvents` | Shut down the event broker connection |

### Typical Pattern

1. Define a Business Event Service with PUBLISH messages
2. Create entities prefixed with `PBE_` that **extend `BusinessEvents.PublishedBusinessEvent`**
3. Entity attributes must **exactly match** the message attributes (no extra attributes on the entity)
4. In microflows, create an instance of the event entity, populate its attributes, commit it
5. Call `BusinessEvents.PublishBusinessEvent_V2` with a `Subject` template and the entity instance as `BusinessEvent`
6. For subscribe operations, link a handler microflow in the service definition

## Checklist

- [ ] Linked entities must exist before creating the service
- [ ] **Entities must extend `BusinessEvents.PublishedBusinessEvent`** (for published events)
- [ ] **Entity attributes must exactly match the message attributes** (no extra/missing attributes)
- [ ] **No message attribute may reuse a name the entity inherits** from `BusinessEvents.PublishedBusinessEvent` (e.g. `EventId`) — an inherited attribute does not count, so mxbuild reports it "not present on the entity". `check -p … --references` reports it
- [ ] Entity names use qualified format: `Module.EntityName`
- [ ] Entities for published events are conventionally prefixed with `PBE_`
- [ ] Attribute types must be valid (String, Integer, Long, Decimal, Boolean, DateTime)
- [ ] Use `describe business event service` to verify the result
- [ ] The DESCRIBE output is parseable and can be used as a CREATE statement
- [ ] To publish events from microflows, use `call java action BusinessEvents.PublishBusinessEvent_V2`
- [ ] The `BusinessEvents` module must be included in the project (marketplace module)

### What `check -p … --references` Reports for a CONSUMER (MDL-BE01..BE07)

mxbuild validates **none** of this: measured on 11.16.1, a consumer whose `consume` names a
message the contract does not contain builds with 0 errors, and the build never looks at the
consumed entity, the handler, the module or the broker constants. The failure is the running
app's — it consumes nothing, silently, or does not boot.

- [ ] **BE01** the contract parses as AsyncAPI 2.x and declares at least one channel (an empty
      one makes mxbuild throw "business events service should have definitions")
- [ ] **BE02** every `consume` names a message in `components.messages` — **case-sensitively**
- [ ] **BE03** the consumed entity is persistent (not a view) and extends
      `BusinessEvents.ConsumedBusinessEvent`; a payload property with no attribute, or an
      attribute whose type no encoding of that property holds, **warns** (the set per encoding
      is in `businessevents.MendixAttributeTypesFor` — a `string` property accepts a `String`,
      an `Enumeration` or a `HashedString`)
- [ ] **BE04** the handler takes exactly one parameter, of the consumed entity or an ancestor
- [ ] **BE05** the `BusinessEvents` module is in the project
- [ ] **BE06** `BusinessEvents.StartupBusinessEvents` is reachable from the after-startup
      microflow, directly or through another microflow — **warns**, because without it the app
      consumes nothing while every other check stays green
- [ ] **BE07** `BusinessEvents.ServerUrl` has a default, and one of `BusinessEvents.ChannelName`
      / `BusinessEvents.EventBrokerSpace` — **warns**, since both are per-environment values
      (`mxcli constant set BusinessEvents.ServerUrl '<broker>:9092'` for a dev run). Measured:
      with either missing the app **fails to boot**
